reflection: Nothing has reached the selected team or the promising list yet, and every factor so far has been weak (average gains near zero, with the sign flipping across years). The clearest pattern is that factors close to existing ones (QQQ_return_1d, MSFT_return_1d, AAPL_volatility_10d, AAPL_cum_return_5d) add no new information, and single-stock ratios are unstable across regimes such as 2024. Factors that carry volatility or peer-lead information should be tried in a different form, not as near-copies. This round I will use a smoothed intraday range for Apple volatility, a longer peer-lead window, a QQQ volume regime, and an intraday return that is distinct from the overnight gap. I will pair factors of different roles so that any joint gain can be checked against the sum of their individual gains.

lessons.name: msft_return_1d_sign
lessons.lesson: It was invalid because sign() produced a constant in at least one training or validation quarter, so the factor carried no usable variation and should be rebuilt as a continuous measure.

lessons.name: aapl_vol10_relative_qqq
lessons.lesson: The ratio of Apple to QQQ 10-day volatility flipped sign between years and was not stable, so it added no reliable signal beyond AAPL_volatility_10d.

lessons.name: aapl_overnight_gap_1d
lessons.lesson: The overnight gap helped only in 2022 and 2025 and hurt in 2024, so its signal is regime-dependent and too unstable to pass the 3-of-4-years bar.

lessons.name: qqq_close_to_ma20
lessons.lesson: It is highly similar to QQQ_cum_return_5d (0.75) and its gains were inconsistent across years, so it mostly repeated existing QQQ trend information.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_nvda_mean_5d
lessons.lesson: The 5-day average of Apple minus NVDA returns is close to NVDA_cum_return_5d (0.81) and mostly restates it, so it adds little new information.

lessons.name: qqq_return_z_10d
lessons.lesson: Dividing QQQ's one-day return by its 10-day volatility produced a near-copy of QQQ_return_1d (0.97) with no added robustness.

factors.name: aapl_intraday_range_smooth_10d
factors.hypothesis: AAPL_volatility_10d is built from close-to-close returns, which are noisy and can be dominated by a single gap day; a 10-day mean of the high-low range uses intraday information instead, so it should be less redundant with the return-based volatility factors and carry a different volatility signal in years such as 2024 when the close-to-close measure failed.

factors.name: msft_cum_return_10d
factors.hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is a single noisy day that helped in some years and not others; a 10-day MSFT return captures a slower peer trend that may lead Apple's next move and is less similar to the existing 1-day and 5-day MSFT returns.

factors.name: qqq_volume_to_ma20
factors.hypothesis: Abnormal volume in the broad tech index signals market-wide participation or stress, which is a market state not represented by any existing factor; it uses QQQ volume rather than Apple volume.

factors.name: aapl_intraday_return
factors.hypothesis: The same-day return from open to close captures intraday buying or selling pressure, which is distinct from the overnight gap that was tested and rejected in round 2.

factors.name: aapl_rel_qqq_cum_10d
factors.hypothesis: Apple's 10-day performance relative to QQQ measures whether Apple is under- or over-performing the market; combined with the volatility level it may show whether relative weakness in a high-volatility regime tends to reverse.

factors.name: qqq_vol_20d
factors.hypothesis: The 20-day realised volatility of the broad market describes the regime in which a one-day MSFT move carries information, so the pair may show that the peer-lead signal works only in calm markets.
